title: Cell Structure and Transport
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Cell Structure and Transport Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: Cells as the basic structural unit of all organisms; similarities and differences between plant and animal cells; eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells; the function of sub-cellular structures; how specialised cells are adapted; the use of light and electron microscopes, magnification and resolution; the importance of cell differentiation; required processes of diffusion, osmosis and active transport across membranes.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on cell structure and transport: eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells, microscopy and magnification, diffusion, osmosis and active transport. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Osmosis moves water; active transport needs energy.
key_sub: Magnification = image size ÷ real size; 1 mm = 1,000 µm.
body_html:
How to think about it

All living things are made of cells.

  • Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus; prokaryotic cells (bacteria) have a loop of DNA and plasmids instead.
  • Magnification = image size ÷ real size. Convert to the same units first (1 mm = 1,000 µm).
  • Diffusion: particles from high to low concentration. Osmosis: water across a partially permeable membrane. Active transport: against the gradient, using energy from respiration.
Example

Image 5 mm, cell 25 µm. Magnification?

5 mm = 5,000 µm

5,000 ÷ 25

Answer: ×200

Example

Mineral ions into a root against the gradient?

Needs energy

Answer: active transport

Common mistakes

  • Thinking bacteria have a nucleus.
  • Dividing real size by image size.
  • Thinking osmosis moves solute particles.

faq.q: What is the difference between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells?
faq.a: Eukaryotic cells (animals, plants, fungi) keep their DNA in a nucleus. Prokaryotic cells (bacteria) are smaller, with a single loop of DNA and small rings called plasmids.
Magnification = image size ÷ real size, with both in the same units. Remember 1 mm = 1,000 µm.

faq.q: What is the difference between diffusion, osmosis and active transport?
faq.a: Diffusion moves particles from high to low concentration. Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane. Active transport moves substances against a concentration gradient and needs energy.
